text:
Noah Kim: Hi all, first-week question — trying to get the local dev stack running. Compose brings up postgres and redis but my app (running on host) can't reach redis on 6379. I tried host localhost:6379 and host.docker.internal:6379, both fail. Docker Desktop says containers healthy. Any common Mac M1 pitfalls?

Rina Patel: Welcome Noah! If the app runs on host, host.docker.internal is the right hostname on mac. If that still fails, check that compose actually maps the port (ports: - "6379:6379"). If you used a named volume or network-only setup with no published ports, host can't see it.

Noah Kim: Compose file didn't publish redis port (we usually rely on internal network). I added ports and now connection times out with ECONNREFUSED. I do have redis installed via brew — could that be conflicting?

Rina Patel: Yep, if brew redis is running it can bind 6379 on host and block the mapping. Run `brew services list` and stop it with `brew services stop redis` or map to a different host port like "16379:6379" and point to host.docker.internal:16379.

DevEx: Also for M1 images: some images default to amd64 and fail subtly. If you see "exec format error" or the container keeps restarting, use an arm64-compatible tag (postgres:15-alpine, redis:7-alpine) or set `platform: linux/amd64` temporarily.

Noah Kim: Thanks — I stopped brew redis, restarted compose, redis connects. One follow-up: my postgres init SQL creates a user and DB, but after mapping ./pgdata it looks like init didn't run. Logs say "skipping initialization". How do I force it to run?

Rina Patel: The entrypoint only runs on an empty data dir. If you mapped a host dir that already has files, it won't re-init. Options: (1) `docker-compose down -v` and remove host dir contents `rm -rf ./pgdata/*`, (2) use a named volume instead, or (3) run a one-off container to drop DB and re-init. Beware of deleting real data.

Noah Kim: Init files were 0640 from my editor. Could permission bits cause entrypoint to skip them?

Rina Patel: The entrypoint reads files as the postgres user. Make sure init scripts are readable: `chmod 644 ./db/init/*` and that they have .sql/.sh extension. Also confirm you mount to `/docker-entrypoint-initdb.d:ro` and the files are visible inside container with `docker run --rm -v $(pwd)/db/init:/docker-entrypoint-initdb.d:ro postgres:15 ls -l /docker-entrypoint-initdb.d`.

ops-bot: Reminder: internal dev docs at https://redwood.internal/dev/local-db-setup include best-practices for Mac M1, port mapping conventions (15xxx), and an example docker-compose.override.yml for running the app in compose to avoid host networking issues.
